source.title: Forward Stability of ResNet and Its Variants

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates held-out natural-label accuracy across network depths, but does not test any listed version’s specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: Clean CIFAR-10/100 test accuracy by depth is reported and recorded as a finding outside the listed versions. Corrupted-test-image results concern perturbation robustness, which the claim excludes. Cited results from prior work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study tests depth and input-corruption effects in proposed ResNet variants, but none of V1–V8. Increasing depth does not test V2's width intervention; forward sensitivity to input perturbations does not test V7's magnitude-scaled weight sharpness and generalization-gap correlation. The sharp-minima discussion cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the experimental findings: average clean accuracy increases with depth, and stronger input corruption reduces accuracy. The authors also establish forward-stability bounds and argue that the variants preserve ResNet-like accuracy. Their proposed connection between improved accuracy, generalization, and optimal-control well-posedness remains an interpretation rather than an experimentally isolated explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes constrained ResNet-D and ResNet-S variants, trains with mini-batch gradient descent, and evaluates test accuracy; does not reproduce the specified claim studies or their measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with depth and dataset; under corruption it varies with corruption type and level, though those results are outside the claim's stated scope.

fits_no_version.finding: Average clean test accuracy increases at every reported depth increment for both variants on both datasets, although some increments are small and uncertainty is not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With the specified fixed training recipes, increasing depth improves average clean test accuracy in ResNet-D and ResNet-S on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision
record.problems: No training accuracy or train-test gap is reported; the authors state hyperparameters were fixed and not tuned. The reported accuracy averages over the last 5,000 steps, with no uncertainty estimates stated.
record.rows_left_out: Corrupted-test-image accuracies in Table 5.4 and Figures 5.3–5.4 are omitted because the claim explicitly separates out-of-distribution and corruption robustness. Figure 5.1's depth curves are not separately rowed because Table 5.3 gives the numerical clean-test results.

untested.parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label training and held-out accuracy.
No width sweep, zero-training-error threshold, or convergence-based comparison beyond that threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or intervention on learned local connectivity.
No optimizer comparison or comparison of tuning budgets.
Batch size is fixed at 128; no large-batch penalty or recipe adaptation is tested.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures. Input sensitivity and speculative flatter-minimum arguments do not measure these.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. All recorded numerical accuracies match the supplied tables. Depth counts unique filters and weights, including one filter per symmetric residual layer. No supplied-version verdict follows from these results.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare random-label and natural-label generalization.
Varies depth, not width, and does not identify an interpolation threshold or report training error.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks.
Does not compare adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
Does not vary batch size or compare large and small batches.
Does not vary dropout or weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with train-test gaps.
Does not remove or retrain on memorized examples.
